segments.note: The Delaware Railroad (chartered 1836, construction begun 1854 after a long delay) opened Wilmington-Dover service by 1856, reached Seaford later that year, and was completed to Delmar at the Maryland line in 1859 — Dover's first rail service. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The New York, Philadelphia and Norfolk Railroad completed the line down Maryland and Virginia's Eastern Shore to Cape Charles in 1884, connecting to a ferry across the mouth of the Chesapeake Bay to Norfolk. Became part of the Pennsylvania Railroad system. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The Del-Mar-Va Express ran daily New York/Philadelphia-Cape Charles from 1926, with car-ferry connection to Norfolk, alongside local trains. Discontinued 1957 with the rest of PRR's Delmarva passenger service; the independent ferry itself ran until 1964, replaced by the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel.
